Welcome to KnuVu

KnuVu is a Competitive Intelligence Platform that takes sourced and internal data and maps each data point to your strategy to provide a multivariate and visually obvious decision-making framework that infuses your Knowledge into an entirely new view, or KnuVu.

Data + Strategy + AI creation and support: we’ve architected KnuVu with BYO Data, AI, Strategy and Vision, so models may begin with a prompt, an import, or connections — and our full-featured Reporting, Wargaming and Scenario modules provide a complete, heavy-lift starting point in minutes. Our Data Truth Hammer and Validation tools ensure the highest level of accuracy and defense against AI drift and hallucination.

Ready to KnuVu Let’s Go!
Or browse the libraries

Start a KnuVu

Describe a landscape to analyze, or ask for a deliverable. Claude builds the model — or the report — from your request.

AI Support:

In production, a landscape prompt runs Autopopulate (§19.4) and a deliverable prompt routes to the Report Builder (§12). Every autogeneration entry point runs the live propose-then-refine generator in place — producing a model from your prompt, with an offline simulator as automatic fallback. The Frontier Labs model remains available as a loadable reference (it’s no longer shown as a generation result).

Weighted Score
Autopopulated by Claude from public benchmark & market reporting (≈ June 2026). Rating mode scores each cell 0–100 on its merits (default); pick a benchmark to grade everyone against one entity. Figures are approximate, vary by source/date, and several are source-linked for live refresh — illustrative of the workflow, not an authoritative ranking. Use AI Support to add dimensions (e.g. consumer sentiment, trust), discover entities, or validate; use Autopopulate to generate a whole new KnuVu from a prompt.
KnuVu nesting map

Scenarios

Re-weight what matters and watch the ranking move. Save named scenarios, tag and group them, share any one as a read-only link, or run a sensitivity sweep to see which dimensions most change the answer. Entities and dimensions are derived from this KnuVu’s canonical model — the same single source of truth the Matrix uses (§21). Changing priorities here never touches the base data.

Wargame

Assign analysts to labs and pressure-test a competitive move. Each seat’s standing is computed live from the canonical model; run a what-if and see who gains.

Scenario player client overlay

The client-facing view. A client can add their own entities and dimensions, re-weight priorities, and compare their thesis against the analyst baseline — all of it a private overlay that never modifies the analyst’s source model (§10, §21).

Report builder

Three layers: Claude auto-drafts from the live model, you edit, then export. The draft below is generated from this KnuVu’s current entities, dimensions and scores.

Data sources

Connect live sources and bind dimensions to them. The benchmark dimensions in this model are already source-linked to public leaderboards and refresh on demand (§20.6).

Fork this model

A fork is your own editable copy of the Frontier Labs model. It inherits every entity, dimension and score; your weight and priority overrides stay local until you publish.

Balanced Scorecard · set up baseline

This template asks a couple of questions once, then seeds the goal-attainment baseline from an industry lookup (Template Intake & Baseline Seeding, §15.3). Targets stay illustrative and fully editable.

Customize toolbar

Drag the handle to reorder (or use the arrows), hide items you don’t use, and add group dividers to keep things tidy. One arrangement is shared by the expanded toolbar and the minimized icon rail. It’s saved per user — it does not travel with the file — and changes apply immediately.

New from template

Each template ships a complete dimension set, category bands, suggested priorities, a legend and palette, and an example entity roster — use it as-is or as a starting point. The matrix generalizes the AT&T methodology to any domain (§15).

Examples

A browsable library of fully worked reference KnuVus, organized by analysis type. Open one to load it as a working model — then save, fork, or use it as a starting point. Folders without examples yet are shown so the full taxonomy is visible.

Defaults apply to new KnuVus; per-model settings live with the model.

Every consequential change, in order (§22)
Autopopulate a KnuVu

Describe the landscape to analyze

Benchmark is a comparative lens: every entity is scored on its merits, and the designated benchmark drives the comparative view (§7.1.1).

1 Researching entities & resolving the competitive set…
2 Proposing dimension categories & priorities (P1–P4)…
3 Pulling benchmarks & market data from live sources…
4 Scoring each cell 0–100 with notes, confidence & volatility…
5 Assembling matrix & legend…

Generation is propose-then-refine (§19.7): a fast skeleton pass proposes the entity set, the categories and the dimensions with P1–P4 priorities — it never asks you for an exact dimension count. You review and edit the proposed set, then KnuVu scores the Active entities. Candidates land in a pool with a fit score; at/above the promotion threshold they’re promoted and scored, below they wait in the pool. The rating is the primary datum; performance and A/B/C are derived from it. Failed bands are retried smaller, then left for Fill gaps. The Active-entity cap and thresholds live in Settings → AI. (Runs inside Claude.ai. Opened from disk the in-app API isn’t reachable, so tick Simulate offline — or it falls back to a simulated model automatically — to stress-test the flow end to end.)

Fires a tiny ping and reports reachable / class / status in AI Support — no full generation.
